name: Sprint-to-Stick Deceleration — 3 m approach
difference: Original Class 1 reference; reserved against repetition.

name: 180-Degree Turn / Shuttle Cut — 3 m in, 3 m out
difference: Original Class 1 reference; reserved against repetition.

name: Lateral Bound to Stick — opposite-leg landing
difference: Original Class 1 reference; reserved against repetition.

name: Lateral Shuffle Decel Stick
difference: Original Class 1 reference; reserved against repetition.

name: Planned Lateral Shuffle Reversal
difference: Original Class 1 reference; reserved against repetition.

name: Crossover Step and Go
difference: Original Class 1 reference; reserved against repetition.

name: Lateral Line Pogo
difference: Repeated bilateral ankle rebounds; unlike Class 1's single-flight opposite-leg bound and grounded shuffles.

name: Shuffle-to-Sprint Transition
difference: Moving lateral entry into an orthogonal running exit, unlike the stationary crossover start or same-facing reversal in Class 1.

name: Lateral Open-Step to Sprint
difference: Near-leg open step replaces Class 1's far-leg crossover; this is a different first contact sequence, not a faster copy.

name: Lateral Hop to Stick — bilateral
difference: Bilateral takeoff and landing with a terminal hold, unlike single-leg bounds or continuous line rebounds.

name: Skater Bound Continuous — one out-and-back pair
difference: Two linked opposite-leg flights with one active rebound; Class 1's bound ends in a static hold.

name: Grounded Lateral Scoop Slam
difference: Grounded externally resisted lateral projection; no earlier ballistic throw slot exists.

name: Paused Split-Stance Diagonal Jump
difference: Paused split-stance two-foot takeoff and shared landing; not the lateral bilateral countermovement jump or unilateral bound.

name: 45-Degree Cut and Reaccelerate
difference: One diagonal planted running cut, distinct from a 180-degree return or shuffle-to-forward gait change.

name: 45-Degree Cut-and-Stick
difference: Terminal control after a diagonal redirection; E2 continues accelerating instead. It is not a second copy at a different speed.

name: Crossover Bound to Stick
difference: A crossover loads one bounded flight and terminal single-leg landing; Class 1's crossover continues running.

name: Split-Step to Diagonal Sprint
difference: Bilateral landing initiates the run, unlike a static start, a run-to-cut or a jump that ends in a hold.

name: Single-Leg Diagonal Hop to Stick
difference: Same-leg takeoff/landing; earlier diagonal jumps share the landing or switch legs.

name: Forward-Back Line Hops
difference: Sagittal forward/back force reversal rather than Class 2's frontal lateral line hops; plane change has a specific braking-support role.

name: Deceleration Re-Acceleration Sprint
difference: Contains a deliberate stopped interval and same-heading restart; Class 1's linear stop ends the attempt and its shuttle reverses direction.

name: Falling Start Acceleration — short exit
difference: A controlled fall initiates movement; it isolates projection from stillness rather than a run-to-stop sequence.

name: Forward Run to Lateral Shuffle
difference: Forward entry becomes lateral shuffle; it reverses the gait relationship of Class 2's shuffle-to-running exit.

name: Forward Hop to Stick — bilateral
difference: Forward bilateral terminal landing; earlier bilateral lateral jumps load a different plane and line hops are continuous elastic work.

name: Single-Leg Forward Hop to Stick
difference: Same-leg sagittal absorption is deliberately separated from oblique/diagonal acceptance; no crossing or lateral plant component.

name: Quarter-Turn Jump to Stick — bilateral
difference: An in-flight bilateral body turn, absent from all previous drills.

name: 90-Degree Speed Cut
difference: A square running corner needs different momentum redirection from the previous 45-degree cut; direction is the deliberate training variable, not a renamed time trial.

name: Shuffle-to-Backpedal Corner
difference: Lateral entry changes to backward gait; earlier transitions ended in forward running or lateral shuffling.

name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop to Stick
difference: Same-leg lateral landing rather than the opposite-leg bound or sagittal/diagonal hop.

name: Lateral Bound to Forward Sprint
difference: The bound landing becomes a running redirection rather than a static hold or return bound.

name: Three-Point Diagonal Start
difference: A hand-supported low start changes initial support and force projection; not the falling or standing crossover start.

name: Backpedal-to-Stick
difference: Backward gait and backward braking replace the forward/lateral terminal stops already used.

name: Backpedal-to-Forward Reversal
difference: Travel reverses while facing stays constant; Class 1's running shuttle required a body turn.

name: Sprint-to-Backpedal Transition
difference: Forward-to-backward gait order contrasts with E2's backward-to-forward task and requires a different first exit action.

name: Backward Two-Foot Jump to Stick
difference: Backward bilateral flight and absorption, absent from the earlier forward/lateral/turning landing tasks.

name: Drop-Step Crossover Go
difference: A drop step precedes the crossover; Class 1 expressly used crossover first with no drop step.

name: Backpedal-to-Sprint Turn — open, same travel heading
difference: Facing changes while travel continues; E2 changes travel while facing stays fixed.

name: Split-Stance Pogo
difference: Fixed staggered bilateral support rather than parallel-foot lateral or forward/back line travel.

name: 135-Degree Running Cut
difference: An obtuse return diagonal differs from the 45-degree continuation, square corner and full 180-degree shuttle; the distinct braking demand justifies the angle-specific drill.

name: Drop-Step Decel Cone Box
difference: One rapid step into a terminal stop; the earlier drop-step drill continued through a crossover into running.

name: Crossover Run to Stick
difference: A moving crossover gait terminates in braking; stationary crossover starts and crossover-to-bound have different contact sequences.

name: Curved Run Decel
difference: Distributed curving entry then terminal deceleration, rather than a straight entry or a discrete cone cut.

name: Rotational Bound to Stick
difference: Unilateral opposite-leg landing with an airborne quarter-turn, distinct from the bilateral quarter-turn jump and non-rotating lateral bound.

name: Lateral Skip — two cycles
difference: Step-hop skip rhythm with repeated same-leg support, unlike bilateral pogos or opposite-leg bounding.

name: Curved Run to Cut
difference: Curved entry is followed by a discrete planted cut; Class 7's curved run only decelerated to a terminal stop.

name: Figure-8 Cone Run
difference: Two opposing continuous loops with an inflection, not a single curved stop or a sharp cone cut.

name: Carioca Quick Hips
difference: Alternating front/behind crossing gait rather than crossover running with only an open forward crossing.

name: Diagonal-to-Lateral Bound Pattern
difference: The two flights change between diagonal and lateral vectors; the earlier skater pair reversed along one lateral line.

name: Shuffle Arc to Running Exit
difference: Continuous curving gait transition rather than Class 2's abrupt orthogonal shuffle-to-sprint corner.

name: W Drill Forward Cuts — short three-leg route
difference: Two linked alternating cuts in one forward course rather than one isolated cut.

name: Z Route — Two Square Corners
difference: Two opposing square cuts joined by a short lateral leg; no previous isolated corner or continuous curve has this route/contact structure.

name: Triangle Shuffle-Sprint Drill
difference: Two running/shuffle transitions around a closed triangle, unlike the all-running W or Z routes.

name: U-Drill Turn-and-Go
difference: Rounded half-loop joining parallel legs instead of the original planted same-line shuttle reversal.

name: Forward Zigzag Bounds — two flights
difference: Both flights retain forward travel with alternating diagonal vectors; earlier pairs returned laterally or switched from diagonal to pure lateral.

name: Split-Stance Rotational Scoop Slam
difference: Rotation from a fixed split base, unlike Class 2's translating lateral weight-shift projection.

name: W Drill Backpedal Cuts — short route
difference: Backward gait through linked changes; Class 9's W used forward running.

name: Box Drill — Sprint, Shuffle, Backpedal
difference: Four sides with three distinct gait transitions, unlike the triangle's two corners or a single transition.

name: X Crossing Route — two obtuse plants
difference: Crossing diagonals linked by a transverse leg create two obtuse plants; neither the W nor Z has this crossing topology.

name: Crossover Run Reversal
difference: Crossing lateral gait enters and leaves the reversal; earlier lateral reversals used non-crossing shuffle contacts.

name: Single-Leg Backward Hop to Stick
difference: Backward same-leg landing instead of the earlier bilateral backward jump or forward/diagonal same-leg hop.

name: Quarter-Turn Single-Leg Hop to Stick
difference: Same-leg landing during the airborne turn, rather than the bilateral quarter-turn or opposite-leg rotational bound.

name: Two-Foot Lateral Jump to Single-Leg Landing
difference: Bilateral takeoff to unilateral landing, not a unilateral bound or a bilateral lateral landing.

name: Planned Lateral Jab-to-Crossover Exit
difference: A weight-bearing false step precedes an opposite-direction crossover exit; previous stationary crossover/drop-step starts did not reverse a jab's momentum.

name: V Shuttle to Opposite Diagonal
difference: One 180-degree turn followed by a 90-degree exit at the shared origin; earlier multi-cut routes used repeated/alternating corner types without this return junction.

name: Two Forward Rebound Jumps
difference: Whole-leg forward rebound with two flights, unlike ankle-only line hops or a forward jump ending in a hold.

name: Single Forward Bound to Running Exit
difference: Forward flight continues into the same-heading run; the earlier lateral bound-to-run required perpendicular redirection.

name: Half-Kneeling Lateral Start
difference: One knee and one foot provide the initial support, unlike standing, falling or hand-supported starts.

name: Gathered Stop-to-Diagonal Restart
difference: A reoriented two-step gather and deliberate pause precede a diagonal restart; earlier stop-restarts stayed straight and earlier diagonal cuts had no static reset.

name: M-Drill Multidirectional Cut — compact course
difference: Four legs and three alternating corner demands, unlike the shorter W/Z/X patterns; the middle valley requires a second reorganization before the last peak.

name: Five-Cone Compass Route — known three-arm sequence
difference: Repeated returns to a shared centre with different outgoing arms; unlike a perimeter course or the two-arm V junction.

name: Three-Hop Directional Pattern — same leg
difference: Three same-leg contacts across three vectors; previous linked bounds alternated legs and ended after two flights.

name: Crossover Run to Backpedal Exit
difference: Crossing-gait entry into backpedal rather than the earlier square shuffle entry or forward-running entry.

name: Single-Leg Lateral Push Jump to Two-Foot Landing
difference: Unilateral paused takeoff to a bilateral landing; earlier lateral tasks used same-leg/opposite-leg landings or bilateral takeoff.
